subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but code review cannot choose whether hosted/team-chat UX should override the current safety default that prevents silent false success for failed writes, sends, or exec actions.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after coverage proves real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep boolean suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and close or narrow the final-only request to docs and channel-specific bugs.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle remaining concrete leaks such as Feishu, read-only exec misclassification, or lifecycle-warning routing in separate issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after coverage proves real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged warning-policy fix that explicitly left this issue open for the broader delivery-policy decision.
